chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Sulaymān ibn Ḥafṣ al-Marwazī, from al-Rajul عليه السلام, who said:
When the boy completes eight years, his affair is valid, and the obligations and prescribed penalties have become binding upon him. And when the girl completes nine years, then likewise.

key_terms.الْجَارِيَةِ: the girl; the female child addressed in the ruling
key_terms.الْحُدُودُ: the prescribed legal penalties and limits in the sacred law
key_terms.الْغُلَامِ: the boy; the male child addressed in the ruling
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضُ: the obligatory duties binding upon a legally responsible person
key_terms.تِسْعُ سِنِينَ: nine years; the age mentioned for the girl
key_terms.ثَمَانُ سِنِينَ: eight years; the age mentioned for the boy
key_terms.جَائِزٌ أَمْرُهُ: his affair is valid; his act or authority is recognized as effective

ai.seo_question: At what age do religious obligations and legal accountability begin for a boy and a girl in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the age at which obligations and prescribed legal consequences apply to a boy and a girl. It is significant in fiqh discussions related to legal responsibility, accountability, and the enforcement of rulings.
